thread:
maya: Heads-up — observed a big tail of late telemetry for EU ingest between 2024-06-01T00:00 and 2024-06-02T04:00. A bunch of aggregates are stale. Thinking we need a coordinated backfill. Anyone on-call for replays?
jordan: I can help. how big are we talking?
maya: Rough estimate ~1.2B events, mostly from partition p-23, affects hourly aggs and KV-cache rehydrate. Cost estimate from last run ~€4k if we rerun naively.
nina: Oof. Do we know why they were late? network blip -> delayed consumer?
maya: root cause is a downstream debounce that dropped a backup topic. Will follow up with infra. For now we have to fix freshness.
eli: Can we do a targeted replay just for the affected tenant slice + hourly buckets instead of full reprocess?
maya: Yes that's my leaning. But console current UX only lets you pick time windows, not fine-grained tenant slices.
jordan: We could run the CLI with a filter:
```
replay --start=2024-06-01T00:00 --end=2024-06-02T04:00 --shard=p-23 --cohort=hourly --tenant-filter=tenant_ids: [acme, beta]
```
But ops would prefer a safer lighter path via console so product/console folks can approve.
sam: Two concerns: quota and routing. If we push this through default priority lane it may evict production queries. We should use a priority lane with capped concurrency.
nina: Agree. Also add preflight estimate in the console so non-ops folks don't accidentally schedule huge replays.
maya: Proposed plan: 1) run a small canary replay for 1 hour of data on p-23, 2) validate aggregates, 3) scale up with fair-share weights and a global cap.
eli: +1. For scaling, scheduler support to pin a backfill to dedicated backfill capacity would help. Right now the routing policy only has cost vs latency; we need a "backfill" affinity.
jordan: Can we implement soft preemption instead of hard? i.e., backfills yield CPU and queue slots but keep progress checkpointed. That reduces tail impact.
sam: Also request an admin flag to mute backfill alerts to SLO on-call while a sanctioned job runs. Today alerts trigger pages.
maya: Yes — mute + annotation in the job metadata. console should show "maintenance backfill" flag.
deploy-bot: Backfill job 736 enqueued by maya (canary) — status: queued.
nina: UX asks: show tokenized estimate and cost in €/USD + expected duration with concurrency knobs. E.g., "Estimated 2.6M rows/hr at 8 workers => ~3h"
jordan: Implementation notes: scheduler needs to accept tags: {backfill:true, affinity:backfill_pool, preemptible:true, fair_weight:0.2} and the console should map the checkboxes to tags.
eli: Also we should rate-limit per-tenant to avoid noisy neighbors. Per-tenant QPS cap + batch-size cap per replay worker.
maya: I'll run the canary, validate aggregates, and share a CSV of golden checks. If green, we'll upscale with these tags.
sam: I'll open a short RFC for (a) console preflight estimate UI, (b) scheduler tags for backfills, (c) alert muting workflow — include migration plan.
nina: Can we also add a small "dry-run" option that runs the planner and emits the cost/time without launching workers? Good for non-ops folks.
jordan: Good idea. CLI + console should support dry-run. The planner can simulate shard counts and return a checksum for expected aggregated deltas.
maya: Canary running now. pinging team when validation done. Thanks all :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: Backfill job 736 status update: running (1/1 canary workers). Approx ETA 12m.
maya: Canary passed basic checks, hourly aggs match golden within noise threshold. Moving to rolling upscale starting 2 workers. I'll tag the job with `backfill:scheduled-by=maya` and `alert-mute=true`.
sam: Please include runbook link in job metadata: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/backfill-blitz
nina: After this, let's sync on console design next week. I'll take ranking for mockups.
maya: Filing follow-ups and RFC — thanks team!
